_comment: Golden fixture for load_discovered_servers (crates/shed-broker/src/discovery.rs) — input ~/.shed/config.yaml text -> expected []ServerTarget. Recorded while the Go daemon still read it; its one reader now is the Rust test golden_load_discovered_servers in crates/shed-broker/src/discovery.rs. Pins the load-bearing divergences from shed-core::ShedConfig: ssh_port defaults to 0 (NOT 22) when omitted, and empty-host entries are skipped. Targets are sorted by name. auth_mode is carried VERBATIM from the entry and is NOT defaulted: "" (never recorded, legacy entry) and "token" (recorded) stay distinguishable, because only the former means "this client has never been told". user (the named user the shed CLI recorded) is carried verbatim (an unquoted scalar is read as its text, as Go's reader reads it: true is the user name "true"); absent or null is "" (no user held); a list or a map is "!not-a-string" (no valid user name, so the entry fails closed instead of reading as no user). identity_file (the SSH key the shed CLI recorded for the entry, plan 037 A8) is carried verbatim, YAML escapes decoded; absent, empty, null or ~ is "" (no key); a list, a map, or a value with a tag or an anchor or over more than one line is the unreadable marker "\u0000<identity_file: not a plain string>" (user: "!not-a-string"), which every check of the value refuses, so the entry fails closed instead of reading as no key; an entry with a merge key (<<) or a key written with a tag (!!str, !!binary) is "\u0000<identity_file: entry not read exactly>" and "!not-a-string" whatever it says. A byte-order mark at the start is skipped and only the first YAML document is read; a raw CR outside a CRLF pair, NEL, U+2028 or U+2029 anywhere makes the whole file an error. auth_mode, user and identity_file are required on every expected entry.

vectors.name: ssh_port default 0, empty-host skipped, api_url vs http fallback, auth_mode carried, sorted
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  https-with-ssh:
    api_url: https://a.example:8443
    host: a.example
    ssh_port: 2222
    auth_mode: mtls
  https-no-ssh:
    api_url: https://b.example:8443
    host: b.example
    auth_mode: token
  plain:
    host: c.example
    http_port: 9000
  empty-host:
    ssh_port: 2222

vectors.name: credentials_token + raw tls_cert_fingerprint carried; ssh_port parsed; default http_port 8080
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  s:
    host: s.example
    ssh_port: 8022
    credentials_token: tok-abc
    tls_cert_fingerprint: sha256:AABBcc

vectors.name: auth_mode is verbatim: an unrecognized value is neither normalized nor rejected
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  weird:
    api_url: https://w.example:8443
    host: w.example
    ssh_port: 2222
    auth_mode: MTLS

vectors.name: user is carried verbatim per entry; absent is empty
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  held:
    api_url: https://h.example:8443
    host: h.example
    ssh_port: 2222
    auth_mode: mtls
    user: pat
  unheld:
    api_url: https://u.example:8443
    host: u.example
    ssh_port: 2222
    auth_mode: mtls

vectors.name: a user that is not a plain string fails closed as !not-a-string, never empty; null is empty; a number is a scalar kept verbatim
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  blockmap:
    host: bm.example
    user:
      name: pat
  flowlist:
    host: fl.example
    user: [pat]
  flowmap:
    host: fm.example
    user: {}
  list:
    host: l.example
    user:
    - pat
  null:
    host: n.example
    user:
  number:
    host: num.example
    user: 5

vectors.name: an unquoted true is read as its text, as Go's reader reads it: the user name true, the same as the quoted value
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  quoted:
    host: q.example
    user: "true"
  unquoted:
    host: u.example
    user: true

vectors.name: identity_file is carried verbatim (YAML escapes decoded); absent, empty, null or ~ is empty; a list or a map fails closed as the unreadable marker; user null or ~ is empty
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  plain:
    host: p.example
    identity_file: /home/pat/.ssh/id_work
  tab:
    host: t.example
    identity_file: "/home/pat/.ssh/id\twork"
  quoted-hash:
    host: q.example
    identity_file: '/home/pat/.ssh/id#work'
  null:
    host: n.example
    identity_file: null
    user: null
  tilde:
    host: ti.example
    identity_file: ~
    user: ~
  bare:
    host: b.example
    identity_file:
  list:
    host: l.example
    identity_file:
    - /home/pat/.ssh/id_work
  map:
    host: m.example
    identity_file: {}

vectors.name: identity_file and user not read exactly fail closed: a tag (!!str null is the string null, never no value), an anchor, or a value over more than one line; an entry with a merge key fails both closed whatever it says; a quoted key is decoded, escapes and all
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  tagged-null:
    host: tn.example
    identity_file: !!str null
    user: !!str null
  tagged:
    host: tg.example
    identity_file: !!str /home/pat/.ssh/id_work
  anchored:
    host: an.example
    identity_file: &key /home/pat/.ssh/id_work
    user: &u pat
  folded:
    host: fo.example
    identity_file: /home/pat/.ssh/first
      second
  merged:
    host: me.example
    <<: {identity_file: /home/pat/.ssh/id_work, user: pat}
  escaped-key:
    host: ek.example
    "identity\u005ffile": /home/pat/.ssh/id_work

vectors.name: every shape of the A8 review's table this reader parses (plan 037 A8; the whole-file errors, an alias, a merge through one and a repeated key, are pinned in discovery.rs's both-readers test): a tagged key (!!str, or !!binary that Go decodes to identity_file) refuses the entry like a merge key; a value with a tag or an anchor, a block scalar or a value continued on an indented line is the unreadable marker; an escaped quoted key, an anchored key, the fields as a flow mapping (on the entry's line or the next) and an explicit ? key are read as Go reads them; a comment after a space or a tab ends the value; a null or ~ host has no target
vectors.config_yaml:
servers:
  escaped-key:
    host: ek.example
    "identity\u005ffile": /keys/prod
  continued:
    host: co.example
    identity_file: /keys/prod
      more
  folded:
    host: fo.example
    identity_file: >-
      /keys/prod
  literal:
    host: li.example
    identity_file: |
      /keys/prod
  tagged-value:
    host: tv.example
    identity_file: !!str /keys/prod
  str-key:
    host: sk.example
    !!str identity_file: /keys/prod
  binary-key:
    host: bk.example
    !!binary aWRlbnRpdHlfZmlsZQ==: /keys/prod
  anchored-value:
    host: av.example
    identity_file: &k1 /keys/prod
  anchored-key:
    host: ak.example
    &k2 identity_file: /keys/prod
  merged:
    host: me.example
    <<: {identity_file: /keys/prod}
  flow-next-line:
    {host: fn.example, identity_file: /keys/prod}
  inline: {host: in.example, identity_file: /keys/prod}
  explicit:
    host: ex.example
    ? identity_file
    : /keys/prod
  null-host:
    host: null
    identity_file: /keys/prod
  tilde-host:
    host: ~
    identity_file: /keys/prod
  comment-space:
    host: cs.example
    identity_file: /keys/prod # the key
  comment-tab:
    host: ct.example
    identity_file: /keys/prod	# the key

vectors.name: the third A8 review's shapes this reader parses (plan 037 A8; the whole-file errors, a raw CR, NEL, U+2028 or U+2029, a second servers: and a tab-indented line, are pinned in discovery.rs's both-readers test): a byte-order mark is skipped; only the first document is read, so a second one cannot replace an entry; a plain name with colons (prod:blue, a:b:c, an address and a port) is read under its own name; a no-break space before a colon makes another key, so that entry has no host and no target
vectors.config_yaml:
﻿servers:
    prod:blue:
        host: blue.example.test
        ssh_port: 2222
        identity_file: /keys/blue
    a:b:c:
        host: abc.example.test
        user: pat
    10.0.0.5:8443:
        host: 10.0.0.5
        ssh_port: 12222
    nbsp:
        host : nbsp.example.test
        ssh_port: 22
---
servers:
    prod:blue:
        host: other.example.test
